clue.text: Tree remained sound, given emergency treatment

parts.note: the fir is a common conifer

indicators.note: sound tells us to take a word as it is said, keeping its pronunciation but changing its spelling

parts.note: remained means stayed

explanation.surface: A tree stayed put while someone was rushed off for urgent medical help.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound' turns the verb for stopping put into its homophone meaning sober and serious; 'given' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Basic medical care given on the spot to an injured person before a doctor arrives is called this.

clue.text: International male singer and female get arrested with nothing on

parts.note: a male is referred to as he

indicators.note: arrested means held in custody, so the word get is held between the singer and the female

parts.note: an alto is a singer with a low voice
a female is referred to as her
taken as written

explanation.surface: A male singer from abroad and a woman are taken into custody while naked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arrested' looks like police action, but it signals the verb held between the singer and the woman. 'with nothing on' is a jokey idiom for naked.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in the altogether is a jokey idiom for being nude.

clue.text: Writer, pious sort leading endless church service

indicators.note: leading means coming in front of the church service that follows

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for saint, a holy person

indicators.note: endless means the final letter of the service is dropped

parts.note: evensong is the evening service in the Church of England

explanation.surface: An author who is a devout person heading a never-ending church service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' trims the last letter of the evening service and 'leading' puts the saint in front. Robert Louis Stevenson wrote Treasure Island.
explanation.definitionFit: Robert Louis Stevenson was the Scottish author of Treasure Island and Kidnapped.

clue.text: Bewildered that search has been scaled down

indicators.note: scaled down means reduced in size, so only a short run of letters inside the following words is kept

explanation.surface: Confused that a search operation has been reduced in scale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has been scaled down' signals a cut-down portion of thAT SEArch.
explanation.definitionFit: Being all at sea is an idiom for being confused and lost.

clue.text: Favourite daughter about to visit far-off lands

indicators.note: to visit means to go into, so the word for about enters the far-off lands

parts.note: the East means distant Asian countries
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A beloved daughter is about to travel to distant countries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to visit' puts the short word for concerning inside the distant lands. 'about to' reads like 'going to', but 'about' is its own piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A most loved person is the one held dearest, a superlative of dear.

clue.text: Wake me, lying in bed with nothing on

indicators.note: in an across clue, on means the next piece is attached after
lying in means the word me rests inside the word for a bed

parts.note: a cot is a small bed
taken as written
nothing is zero, shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: Someone is urged to rouse the speaker, who is lying in bed naked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lying in' puts the speaker inside the small bed and 'on' adds the zero at the end. 'with nothing on' suggests nudity, a deliberate false picture.
explanation.definitionFit: To come to is to regain consciousness, as one does on waking.

clue.text: Permission to proceed in space?

definitions.meaning: official approval to go ahead, as given to an aircraft
the gap or headroom left between two things

explanation.surface: Asking whether an astronaut has been given the go-ahead to launch.
explanation.definitionFit: Approval for take-off is given by air traffic control, and the gap under a bridge is its headroom.

clue.text: Deserve luxury car: it replaces cycle

indicators.note: replaces means the word it is swapped in for the letter standing for cycle

parts.note: Merc is short for a Mercedes, a luxury car
C is the abbreviation for cycle, as in Hz cycles
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone should earn a luxury car, now that it has taken over from their bicycle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it replaces cycle' swaps the C (cycle) in MERC for IT.
explanation.definitionFit: To be worthy of a reward is to earn it.

clue.text: Unbelievably brilliant arrangement of Shaw title

indicators.note: an arrangement rearranges the parts, here the words of the play's name

parts.note: Too True to Be Good is a 1932 play by George Bernard Shaw

explanation.surface: A rearranged version of a Shaw play title is considered a brilliant idea.
explanation.walkthrough: Shaw's play Too True to Be Good has its words reordered to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Something so excellent it seems impossible is said to be unreal.

clue.text: Book accommodation in dream hotel, posh beyond recognition

indicators.note: something changed beyond recognition has been completely rearranged, so these letters are reshuffled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone reserves a room in a dreamy hotel that has gone posh beyond recognition.
explanation.walkthrough: DREAM HOTEL POSH, mixed up 'beyond recognition', gives the title of Lynne Reid Banks's 1960 novel. 'accommodation in' links the definition to the wordplay and also nods to the room in the title.
explanation.definitionFit: Lynne Reid Banks's 1960 novel, set in a London bedsit, has this title.

clue.text: Dog, and what it might do about middle of walkies?

indicators.note: about means the word for urinating goes around the next letter

parts.note: what a dog might do on a walk is pee

indicators.note: middle of picks the central letter of the seven-letter word walkies

explanation.surface: A dog out for its walk, and what it might do halfway round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'middle of' takes K, the centre of WALKIES, and 'about' puts PEE around it. The surface makes this a cheeky picture of the dog in mid-walk.
explanation.definitionFit: A Pekingese, a small long-haired toy breed, is often shortened to this.

clue.text: Mistake made by Republican helping to back former president

indicators.note: to back here means to come behind, so these pieces follow the president's name

parts.note: Abe is Abraham Lincoln, a former US president
a helping or portion of food is a ration

explanation.surface: A Republican's blunder in supporting an ex-president.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to back' only means coming after Lincoln's nickname. 'back' looks like political support for a candidate, but it merely fixes the order.
explanation.definitionFit: A deviation from what is correct or normal is an error or lapse.

clue.text: Those indisposed with flu put on weight

indicators.note: indisposed means out of sorts, so the letters are put in disorder

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: People unwell with influenza have apparently gained weight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'indisposed' looks like illness that goes with 'flu', but it signals that THOSE and FLU are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: To flesh out something is to fill it out and give it more substance, as with an idea or a body.

clue.text: Never stop exercising and you'll get exhausted

indicators.note: exercising means working or moving about, so the letters are moved around

explanation.surface: Advice that constant exercise will leave you worn out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exhausted' looks like physical tiredness, but it means used up, as money is. 'exercising' signals that NEVER STOP is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Exhausted funds have been used up, as a budget is by spending too much.

clue.text: Diarist's terse criticism of wine?

definitions.meaning: the diarist is Charles Pooter of the Grossmiths' comic novel The Diary of a ..., so he is the book's title figure
a curt verdict on a thin wine says it lacks body

explanation.walkthrough: Read as a phrase, the answer is two words, NO BODY, a wine taster's short put-down.
explanation.definitionFit: Pooter is the insignificant person of the Grossmiths' book title, and a thin wine is said to lack fullness.

clue.text: Not a safe place for bacteria

definitions.meaning: a spot on the roads with many accidents
a plant disease marked by dark patches, some forms caused by bacteria

explanation.surface: A warning that somewhere is a dangerous spot for germs.
explanation.definitionFit: A road with a high accident rate earns this label, and it also names a plant disease that blotches leaves.

clue.text: First sign of prey, and wild cat might ---

definitions.text: First sign of prey, and wild cat might ---

indicators.note: first sign of picks the opening letter of the word prey

parts.note: the ounce is another name for the snow leopard

explanation.surface: A wild cat catching the first glimpse of its prey and leaping.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: P, the start of 'prey', plus OUNCE (snow leopard) is what such a cat does on seeing prey.
explanation.definitionFit: To spring suddenly on a victim is what a hunting cat does.

clue.text: Cabinet-maker engaged by furnisher at once

indicators.note: engaged by means held inside the following words, whose letters run across them

explanation.surface: A cabinet-maker hired on the spot by a furniture retailer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'engaged by' looks like employment, but it means the answer sits inside furniSHER AT ONce.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Sheraton was an 18th-century English designer of furniture.

clue.text: Makes a mistake, giving young person drink

parts.note: a slip of a girl is a slight young person
to sup is to drink

explanation.surface: Someone errs by giving a youngster alcohol.
explanation.definitionFit: Slipping up is an idiom for making an error.

clue.text: Cook prepared this with Edam (about one pound)

indicators.note: about means the rearranged letters go around the pound and one
prepared means made ready or worked up, so the letters are remade

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
L is the abbreviation for a pound (from Latin libra)
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A recipe for a dish made with roughly a pound of Edam cheese.
explanation.walkthrough: 'prepared' rearranges the two words into DEASMITH, and 'about' wraps that around the pound and the one. Delia Smith is a famous British TV cookery writer.
explanation.definitionFit: Delia Smith is a best-selling British cookery writer and television chef.

clue.text: Hint just disregarded at the outset

indicators.note: disregarded at the outset means the opening letter is ignored

parts.note: just means simply, as in just wonderful

explanation.surface: A suggestion was simply ignored right from the start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disregarded at the outset' drops the S from SIMPLY.
explanation.definitionFit: To suggest something indirectly is to hint at it.

clue.text: Ambassador needs skill and courage

parts.note: HE stands for His or Her Excellency, the title of an ambassador
art means skill, as in the art of persuasion

explanation.surface: A diplomat needs both talent and bravery.
explanation.walkthrough: An ambassador is addressed as His Excellency, abbreviated HE.
explanation.definitionFit: Having the heart for a fight means having the nerve or bravery for it.

clue.text: Was acquainted with Steinbeck's last novel

indicators.note: last picks the final letter of the name Steinbeck

parts.note: novel as an adjective means new

explanation.surface: Someone was familiar with the final book John Steinbeck wrote.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' looks like a book, which fits Steinbeck, but here it is the adjective meaning new.
explanation.definitionFit: Knowing a person or thing in the past tense is having been familiar with it.

clue.text: Pup — dog with tail docked-runs to man with camera

indicators.note: a docked tail is cut short, so the last letter of the dog is removed

parts.note: a whippet is a slim racing dog
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
a snapper is a slang word for a photographer

explanation.surface: A puppy, a short-tailed dog and a photographer race about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with tail docked' cuts the final letter from the racing dog. 'Pup' here is a cheeky young person, not a young dog, and 'man with camera' is slang for a photographer.
explanation.definitionFit: A cheeky, presumptuous young person is called a pup or upstart.

clue.text: Author taking a little time near ancient city

parts.note: Troy is the ancient city of Homer's Iliad
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A writer spends a short while close to an ancient city.
explanation.walkthrough: Henri Troyat was a Russian-born French novelist and biographer.
explanation.definitionFit: Henri Troyat was a prize-winning French writer of novels and biographies.

clue.text: Staple food and miscellaneous pots o' tea

indicators.note: miscellaneous means mixed and assorted, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
the shortened of gives the letter O
taken as written

explanation.surface: Basic provisions alongside various pots of tea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'miscellaneous' signals that POTS O' TEA is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Spuds are a basic carbohydrate eaten daily in many countries.
